name: Freedoms Foundation at Valley Forge

summary.text: Freedoms Foundation at Valley Forge was founded in 1949 by advertising executive Don Belding of Foote, Cone & Belding, stockbroker Edward F. Hutton of E. F. Hutton & Company, and Kenneth D. Wells, then director of operations of the Joint Committee on Economic Education; the foundation also lists Dwight D. Eisenhower as a co-founder. Eisenhower presented its first National Awards to 200 recipients in 1949 and is variously described as its president, chairman or chairman emeritus until his death in 1969.

facts.claim: The National Park Service's Valley Forge history names Don Belding of Foote, Cone & Belding, Edward F. Hutton of E. F. Hutton & Company and Kenneth D. Wells as the founders in 1949.
facts.quote: Don Belding, of the Los Angeles advertising firm of Foote, Cone & Belding; Edward F. Hutton, of E. F. Hutton & Company in New York; and Kenneth D. Wells

facts.claim: The foundation's own site lists Kenneth D. Wells, Don Belding, General Dwight D. Eisenhower and E.F. Hutton as original co-founders and says Eisenhower presented 200 recipients with the first Freedoms Foundation National Awards in 1949.
facts.quote: original co-founders Kenneth D. Wells, Don Belding, General Dwight D. Eisenhower, and E.F. Hutton

facts.claim: A February 1953 foundation letter in the TCU repository describes efforts to establish budget funds through a National Expansion Committee and names Johns-Manville's Lewis H. Brown and Guy M. Rush as early leaders.
facts.quote: wise guidance and strong cooperation of Directors and friends are essential in this year's work to establish budget funds equal to the needs

sources.title: Freedoms Foundation at Valley Forge letter, February 1953

openQuestions: Corporate donor lists for the 1950s awards program were not found in opened sources; the Eisenhower Library finding aids and the foundation's annual reports would hold them. Sources disagree on whether Eisenhower's title was president, chairman or chairman emeritus. Billy Graham is listed among 1954 award recipients in a 1955 foundation booklet.
